title: Promenade (tempo, text, rehearsal marks)

expected.notes: One oboe staff, D major, 16 bars on 4 systems, 4/4 -> 6/8 (bar 9) -> 4/4 (bar 13). Boxed rehearsal letters A-D at bars 1, 5, 9, 13; bold tempo marks "Allegretto (q = 112)", "Meno mosso" (text only), "dotted-q = 60" (metronome only), "Tempo I (q = 112)"; italic expression text above and below the staff (dolce, espress., rit., leggiero, poco rit., cantabile, allargando, morendo). Text must not become lyrics or notes. Every staff is exactly one part with one voice; double stops / piano chords must stay chords and the piano grand staff must stay one part, so no staff may be split into several parts

notes: Truth encoding: Encoding conventions (also listed in every meta.json 'notes'): * articulations: staccato, staccatissimo, accent, tenuto, strong-accent (marcato; type="up" = ^ above, "down" = v below), detached-legato (portato), breath-mark "comma" on the note the breath mark follows * ornaments: trill-mark, mordent (LilyPond \mordent, with the vertical stroke), inverted-mordent (\prall, no stroke), turn, inverted-turn (\reverseturn) * fermata type="upright" (above) / "inverted" (below); placement of articulations / ornaments / fingerings = the side LilyPond engraved (read back from the grobs) * fingering in <technical>, on the note it belongs to; arpeggiate on every note of the chord * dynamics / wedges / pedal / words / tempo / rehearsal as <direction> placed before the note at whose onset they are engraved (wedge stop = the note where the hairpin ends; LilyPond ends a hairpin at the next dynamic or \!). Pedal marks in LilyPond's default text style ("Ped." / "*") are <pedal type="start|stop" line="no" sign="yes"/>; a "*Ped." change is stop + start. * tempo marks: <words font-weight="bold"> + <metronome> (parentheses="yes" when the text and the number are both printed) + <sound tempo> in quarter notes per minute; expression text: <words font-style="italic">; rehearsal marks <rehearsal enclosure="square"> * score-wide marks (tempo, rehearsal) are written once, in the part whose staff carries them in the engraving (the top staff) * chord symbols: <harmony> with root / kind / bass; kind@text = the printed suffix, or use-symbols="yes" for LilyPond's symbol forms (major-seventh triangle, diminished circle, half-diminished slashed circle, augmented +) * <stem> as engraved (read back from LilyPond), accidentals as LilyPond's default style prints them, <beam> on every note of a beamed chord (levels as engraved, manual beaming)

placement="above|below" of every articulation, ornament and fingering, fermata upright/inverted and marcato (strong-accent) type up/down are the sides LilyPond actually engraved (read back from the final grob directions), not a convention; MusicXML cannot express the exact offset or stacking order of several marks on one note, nor the horizontal position of a fingering inside a chord.

Hairpin extents: LilyPond ends a hairpin at the note carrying \! or the next dynamic; the truth puts <wedge type="stop"/> before that note, so a hairpin "to the barline" is encoded as ending on the next note.  Hairpins crossing a system break are one wedge in the truth.
counting_rules: note-<type>, dot, double-dot, ledger-above/below, acc-*, tie, fingering: per notehead (<note>)
chord, stem-up/down, flag, arpeggio, articulations, ornaments, fermata, slur: per stem/chord event
beam: per beam group (<beam number="1">begin</beam> on the first note of a chord)
rest-*: per rest (<rest measure="yes"/> -> rest-whole-bar), rest-dotted: dotted rests
clef-*, key-*, time-*: per element in the truth (per part; clefs per staff); *-change: elements after the first of that kind in the part/staff

dyn-*, hairpin-*, pedal, text-expression, tempo-mark, metronome, rehearsal-mark: per <direction> child (per hairpin start; pedal releases "*" are counted separately as x-pedal-release); tempo-mark = bold <words> (the engraved tempo text), text-expression = other <words>
chord-symbol: per <harmony>; system-break / page-break: per <print new-system|new-page> of the first part (once per score)
ledger-above / ledger-below: noteheads that need at least one ledger line above / below the staff (from the clef in force)
tie-across-system: tie starting on the last note of a measure that ends a system

validation.method: LilyPond 2.24 event/grob dump (_tools/msynth/dump.ly) compared with the model the truth is written from: every note/rest (onset, pitch, type, dots), tie, beam, slur, articulation/ornament/fermata (with forced direction), dynamic, hairpin start/stop, pedal event, fingering (incl. inside chords), text script, arpeggio, breath mark, tempo and rehearsal-mark event and chord-name pitch content; printed grob counts per kind; printed accidentals; stem directions read from the engraving; MIDI attacks; music21 re-parse; xmllint XSD; symbol counts recomputed from truth.musicxml == model.
